equatags

‘equatags’ transforms LaTeX math expressions:

  • into HTML and into Office Open XML Math, the format of equations in Word and PowerPoint documents, with transform_mathjax();
  • into sizes and drawings: equation_size() computes the width, height and depth of equations and equation_grob() draws them with ‘grid’.

The documentation site has two articles: Equations in Word, PowerPoint and HTML (insertion with ‘officer’, inline and display styles, size and colour) and Size and drawing of equations (alignment on a baseline, ‘ggplot2’, ‘flextable’).

Installation

You can install the released version from CRAN:

install.packages("equatags")

or the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ardata-fr/equatags")

Office Open XML Math and HTML 

cat(transform_mathjax("x^2", to = "mml"))
#> 
#> <m:oMath xmlns:m="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/math">
#>   <m:sSup>
#>     <m:e>
#>       <m:r>
#>         <m:t>x</m:t>
#>       </m:r>
#>     </m:e>
#>     <m:sup>
#>       <m:r>
#>         <m:t>2</m:t>
#>       </m:r>
#>     </m:sup>
#>   </m:sSup>
#> </m:oMath>

With to = "html", the result is the HTML of ‘KaTeX’, to be displayed with its CSS. The ‘Office Open XML Math’ output can be inserted in Word documents with the package ‘officer’ (or ‘flextable’); see the argument rpr of transform_mathjax() to set the size or the colour of equations.

Size and drawing of equations

Equations are laid out with the rules of TeX and the parameters of the ‘MATH’ table of an OpenType math font. The default font is ‘STIX Two Math’, shipped with ‘gdtools’: the results only depend on this file, not on the graphic device or the machine.

equation_size(
  c("\\frac{a+b}{c}", "\\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^2", "\\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}"),
  size = 12, display = TRUE
)
#>       width    height     depth
#> 1 0.4129074 0.2241667 0.1086667
#> 2 0.3778944 0.2637333 0.1801333
#> 3 0.6443407 0.1735583 0.0372750

equation_grob() draws an equation with ‘grid’ (R >= 4.3), with the size computed:

library(grid)
grid.newpage()
grid.draw(
  equation_grob(
    "f(x) = \\frac{1}{\\sigma\\sqrt{2\\pi}} e^{-\\frac{(x-\\mu)^2}{2\\sigma^2}}",
    size = 16, display = TRUE
  )
)

Example with flextable

‘flextable’ uses ‘equatags’ to write equations in HTML, Word and PowerPoint outputs, and to compute their sizes (autofit(), gen_grob()).

library(flextable)

eqs <- c(
  "(ax^2 + bx + c = 0)",
  "a \\ne 0",
  "x = {-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2-4ac} \\over 2a}")
df <- data.frame(formula = eqs)

ft <- flextable(df)
ft <- mk_par(
  x = ft, j = "formula",
  value = as_paragraph(as_equation(formula)))
ft <- align(ft, align = "center", part = "all")
ft <- autofit(ft)
ft

Related work

  • Packages texPreview written by Jonathan Sidi, “compile snippets of ‘LaTeX’ directly into images from the R console to view in the ‘RStudio’ viewer pane, Shiny apps and ‘RMarkdown’ documents”. With this package, you can get images from your ‘latex’ code. The tool offers a wider functional spectrum than just equation processing and focuses on ‘latex’ instead of only ‘MathJax’ equations.

  • Package mathjaxr written by Wolfgang Viechtbauer, “Using ‘Mathjax’ in Rd Files”. This package let you add equations in the manual pages of your package in a very convenient way.

  • Package katex written by Jeroen Ooms, “Rendering Math to HTML, ‘MathML’, or R-Documentation Format”. ‘equatags’ mainly uses its functions.
